nodes.name: Winter snowpack
nodes.desc: Deep winter snow drives elk, moose and pronghorn down from the high country to the valley floor, and its spring melt feeds the Snake River.

nodes.name: Snake River and wetlands
nodes.desc: Rises on the Yellowstone Plateau and runs through the valley, with side channels and wetlands such as Willow Flats and Oxbow Bend that support willow, cottonwood and aspen.

nodes.name: Wildfire
nodes.desc: Burns renew conifer forest and aspen stands. Park agencies now use fire management plans after earlier suppression reduced plant diversity.

nodes.name: Soil nutrients
nodes.desc: Nutrients in valley and sagebrush soils that plants draw on, replenished by decomposers.

nodes.name: Big sagebrush
nodes.desc: The shrub of the sagebrush flats, the most widespread habitat in the park and home to about 100 grass and wildflower species.

nodes.name: Bunchgrasses and sedges
nodes.desc: Native grasses and sedges that grow among the sagebrush and in wet meadows, grazed by elk and bison.

nodes.name: Willows
nodes.desc: Shrubs along the river and wetlands such as Willow Flats, and a main winter and summer browse for moose.

nodes.name: Quaking aspen
nodes.desc: A leafy tree of the valley slopes and river terraces, eaten by elk, moose and beaver.

nodes.name: Elk
nodes.desc: Migrates between summer range in Yellowstone and the surrounding forests and winter range on the National Elk Refuge, passing through the park. Eats mostly sedges, forbs and tree sprouts in summer.

nodes.name: Moose
nodes.desc: Browses willow and eats aquatic plants, and stays near waterways and wetlands in the park.

nodes.name: Pronghorn
nodes.desc: Eats a wide mix of forbs, shrubs and grasses on the open sagebrush flats. Prey for coyotes, wolves and bears.

nodes.name: Mule deer
nodes.desc: A browser of shrubs and wildflowers, recorded eating fireweed and thimbleberry.

nodes.name: American bison
nodes.desc: A large grazer of the valley meadows and sagebrush flats.

nodes.name: American beaver
nodes.desc: Cuts aspen and willow along the river and builds dams that create ponds and wetlands.

nodes.name: Uinta ground squirrel
nodes.desc: Common on the valley floor, eats plants and seeds and is prey for coyotes, eagles and bears.

nodes.name: Mormon cricket
nodes.desc: A flightless shrub-dwelling katydid that eats plants and is eaten by bears and birds.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: Hunts ground squirrels and young hoofed animals and scavenges carcasses.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: Scavenges carcasses, including wolf kills, and eats insects and small prey.

nodes.name: Bald eagle
nodes.desc: Takes waterbirds and small mammals and scavenges carrion along the river.

nodes.name: American black bear
nodes.desc: Omnivore that eats plants, insects and young animals, and scavenges carcasses.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: Returned to the park from Yellowstone after being wiped out in the early 1900s. Preys on elk and moose, with moose calves and weak animals most at risk.

nodes.name: Grizzly bear
nodes.desc: Eats army cutworm moths, roots, berries, pine seeds and carcasses, and takes elk calves.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, animals and dung, returning nutrients to the soil.
